title: WPSS/703/2023 of KIRTI PAL AGARWALA Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 703 of 2023
Kirti Pal Agarwala ........Petitioner

Present:-
Mr. Devesh Bishnoi, Advocate for the petitioner.
Ms. Menka Tripathi, D.A.G. with Mr. Narayan Dutt, Brief
Holder for the State.
Mr. T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Mohd. Shafy,
Advocate for the respondent nos.2 and 3.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 By means of the instant petition, the petitioner
seeks the following reliefs:-
 "(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus calling for the
records relating to the meeting of the
Departmental Promotion Committee
(DPC) for the post of Executive
Director/General Manager, held on
24.06.2009.
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the
respondent no.1 to promote the petitioner
to the post of Executive Director/General
Manager retrospectively, from the date

2
when person junior to him was promoted
to the said post.
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the
respondent no.3 to re-fix the pay of the
petitioner with effect from the date of
grant of promotion as Executive
Director/General Manager and pay the
arrears of difference in pay, including
Gratuity, Leave Encashment &
employer's contribution to the Provident
Fund on the enhanced part of the pay,
for the period from the date where from
the promotion is being granted till the
date of his superannuation, i.e.
31.07.2013.
(iv) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus directing the
respondent no.3 to pay the interest @
12% on the arrears of difference in pay
for the period that the payment has been
delayed.

3
(v) Issue any other writ, order or
direction, which this Hon'ble Court may
deem fit and proper in the facts and
circumstances of the case.
(vi) Award the cost of the present writ
petition to the petitioner."
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record. Learned counsel for the petitioner
appeared through video conferencing.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that he was
initially appointed in the State of Uttar Pradesh and after
creation of the State of Uttarakhand, he gave his option to
serve in the State of Uttarakhand. He had been working
as a Chief Accountant with the respondent no.3. In the
year 2009, process for promotion to the post of Executive
Director/General Manager was undertaken by the
respondent no.3, but, according to the petition, the
petitioner was not considered for the post. Instead, his
junior was considered. The petitioner had already retired
from the services in the year 2013. Now, he claims that he
should be granted promotion as Executive
Director/General Manager, and is also entitled to the

4
consequential reliefs in terms of enhancement of salary,
etc. The Departmental Promotion Committee ("DPC") was
held on 24.06.2009.
4. The Court, at the very outset, asked learned
counsel for the petitioner to explain as to how after 14
years, the issue of promotion should be settled? Is it not
inordinate delayed claim? Learned counsel for the
petitioner very fairly submits that although the claim is
little delayed, but, he would submit that as per
instructions, in between, there has been no promotion.
He would submit that learned Senior Counsel for the
respondent nos. 2 and 3 may be in a better position to tell
as to what is the status of promotional exercise post DPC
dated 24.06.2009.
5. Learned Senior Counsel appearing for the
respondent nos. 2 and 3 would submit that the
petitioner's claim has rightly been not considered for
promotion because he was awarded censure entry in the
year 2008. He was also kept suspended for a while.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner would
submit that the censure entry was subsequently removed.

5
7. The most efficient part of the system would be
if the claims are decided on merits. But, then, delay and
latches has its own space in the judicial system. A claim
made after inordinate delay, when it may have serious
repercussions on the rights and interests of other
persons, who have intervened in between, should not be
entertained.
8. In the case of Union of India and Others Vs.
Tarsem Singh, (2008) 8 SCC 648, the Hon'ble Supreme
Court has summed up the principles on delay and latches
and in Para 7, summarised the position as follows:-
 "7. To summarise, normally, a belated service related
claim will be rejected on the ground of delay and
laches (where remedy is sought by filing a writ
petition) or limitation (where remedy is sought by an
application to the Administrative Tribunal). One of
the exceptions to the said rule is cases relating to a
continuing wrong. Where a service related claim is
based on a continuing wrong, relief can be granted
even if there is a long delay in seeking remedy, with
reference to the date on which the continuing wrong
commenced, if such continuing wrong creates a
continuing source of injury. But there is an
exception to the exception. If the grievance is in
respect of any order or administrative decision which
related to or affected several others also, and if the
reopening of the issue would affect the settled rights
of third parties, then the claim will not be
entertained. For example, if the issue relates to
payment or refixation of pay or pension, relief may be
granted in spite of delay as it does not affect the
rights of third parties. But if the claim involved
issues relating to seniority or promotion, etc.,
affecting others, delay would render the claim stale
and doctrine of laches/limitation will be applied.

6
Insofar as the consequential relief of recovery of
arrears for a past period is concerned, the principles
relating to recurring/successive wrongs will apply.
As a consequence, the High Courts will restrict the
consequential relief relating to arrears normally to a
period of three years prior to the date of filing of the
writ petition."
9. Not only this, in the case of P.S.
Sadasivaswamy Vs. State of Tamil Nadu, (1975) 1 SCC
152, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has, in fact, suggested a
period of six months, or at the most 1 year, for claiming
the promotion. In Para 2 of the judgment, the Hon'ble
Supreme Court observed as hereunder:-
 "2. ........................................................................
..............................................................................
..............................................................................
A person aggrieved by an order of promoting a junior
over his head should approach the Court at least
within six months or at the most a year of such
promotion. It is not that there is any period of
limitation for the Courts to exercise their powers
under Article 226 nor is it that there can never be a
case where the Courts cannot interfere in a matter
after the passage of a certain length of time. But it
would be a sound and wise exercise of discretion for
the Courts to refuse to exercise their extraordinary
powers under Article 226 in the case of persons who
do not approach it expeditiously for relief and who
stand by and allow things to happen and then
approach the Court to put forward stale claims and
try to unsettle settled matters. The petitioner's
petition should, therefore, have been dismissed in
limine. Entertaining such petitions is a waste of time
of the Court. It clogs the work of the Court and
impedes the work of the Court in considering
legitimate grievances as also its normal work. We
consider that the High Court was right in dismissing
the appellant's petition as well as the appeal."

7
10. In the instant case, the petitioner claims that
denial of promotion to him by the DPC on 24.06.2009 was
not correct. He retired in the year 2013. And now he
claims his promotion in the year 2023. It is much
delayed. On this ground, the petition should not be
entertained. Accordingly, the writ petition deserves to be
dismissed at the stage of admission itself.
11. The writ petition is dismissed in limine.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 19.05.2023
Ravi Bisht
